text: I would never recommend this product. If you are completely bald it probably would work. But if you have hair and have a bald spot here or there, don't use it. It has completely ruined my hair. I have lost a lot of hair, the ends are breaking off and look like fuzz. My hair is worse than when I started it. Also, they state if you want resul ts you have to use it for the rest of your life. How that would work without getting it on your hair, I have no idea.

For me although not bald at all, just thinning hair, I found it did not grow back hair that had been lost, but merely stopped or lessened the thinning somewhat, I am over 65 and am not supposed to be using it, although I have had no real side effects at all, but I only use it once a day instead of twice as directed.
It will make your hair fall out! And you may never get it back. Depending on the cause of your hair loss it may not help you at all.

Consider what's more important: hair or permanent health loss.

After getting advice from mu doctor, I started using store brand minoxidil 5% foam on July 19, 2023. I have an alarm set on my phone so I won't forget to apply it. My sister recommended the foam. I’ve been using it for 1 year and I have at least half of what I lost back. Still seeing new growth. Started out using half a cap and now use 1/4 to maintain. It really does work for me. At month 4 I looked like I needed a lawn mower on top of my head. I’m at 6 months and it just keeps coming! It did make my face and eyes swell when I used the recommended dose, so I cut back to about half. Still works! I use kirkland brand generic minoxidil.

I used Minoxidil 5% for 6 months. I may have continued if not for the side effects. From that perspective I actually lost hair, which I know is part of its usage (some shedding etc) but there was no gain in the entire period. The other issue was changes to blood pressure, dizziness, fainting feelings, and foggy brain. These increased and became more severe and even persisted for 2 months after stopping the use. The "faint" feelings became quite intense in that I would get 'rushes' of feeling fai nt/dizzy many times throughout the day. From my experience certainly not recommended. 54 year old male, European, fair hair.

I’m getting married and bought hers regrowth serum with Minoxidil to thicken up my thinning hair for the wedding. The first time I used it I immediately felt really dizzy but brushed it off as something else. The next few days I struggled with lack of sleep, shortness of breath and almost fainted at a client lunchI actually have a history of fainting, like a lot, so that didn’t really tip me off either. A few days later after working out, my resting heart was up to 116 (I workout a TON so my resting heart rate is NEVER that high) and wouldn’t go back down no matter what I tried. I originally thought that was from stress (wedding planning lol) and I took a few days off to relax. I didn’t keep up my normal routine (including applying hers twice a day) just relaxed and of course started to feel normal again. Once I was ready to get back to life (and started using hers again) the same issues came back.only then did I realize that this was a side effect of the solution and not stress!!! I’ve never felt so awful and will never use it again. It’s honestly surprising to me that it’s just sold over the counter at target. I’m obviously fine now but I’m pretty self aware and it still took me like 2 weeks to catch on to what was causing all of this. Thankful nothing worse happened.

I'm 70 years old, have always had fine but plentiful healthy hair, but my new hairdresser said something about my "thinning" hair.Did not want to take pills or supplements, so I bought the 2% solution and applied it 2x a day, using a q-tip to apply at the crown of my head, maybe 4 " by 6" area. They were about 1/4 in long when I was first able to see them, now about 1/2 in. and continuing to grow, so I'll keep up the applications and see what they develop into after maybe 6 months. No little or new hair growth along my grey hairline, however. Results aren't instant, and I don't know how pictures and testimonials can say anything about noticeable results after just 3 or 4 weeks of use they must have very fast growing hair. I also applied a light amount to my eyebrows same thing, now have a few blonde hairs growing in among the regulars. I would never apply to eyelashes, etc. Only complaint: I bought the 3-pack of 2% that had a Rogaine coupon on the box, and could not figure out how to redeem online as required. Seems the R company just wants new customers to subscribe to their online regular deliveries of the product, then maybe they give you a refund. I don't appreciate that kind of customer treatment and duplicity. Other than that, the product worked for me. Try the q-tip for easier application. It helped me with the otherwise messy dripping solution problem.

I want to clarify what I said in my review. I said minoxidil only works if you have a diagnosis of female pattern hair loss. I meant if you are a woman. If you are a man, I suspect the diagnosis would be male pattern hair loss.

first of all, you do need to see a dermatologist to find out the reason for your hair loss. My dermatologist diagnosed female pattern hair loss (I am a woman). this is the only type of hair loss minoxidil (Rogaine) is meant to treat. I used The 5% foam for women. The directions say to put half a capful of foam in a container and then transfer it to your scalp.. This is so you get the idea of how much to use. Once you have the idea, you are much better off spraying it directly onto your s calp instead of trying to transfer it from another container. It will melt and you will have a lot of waste. Follow the directions carefully. I have been using it for five months and have seen A dramatic difference! You have to be consistent. The 5% foam is meant to be used once a day every day. If you stop using it, your hair regrowth will go away.

My barber commented on my receding hairline 4 months before my 18th birthday. I hadn't noticed it myself until and he said I was going to be completely bald by the time I was 20. I'd say I was 2 on the Norwood Scale. After having pretty bad acne through out my early / mid teen years and just about clearing up now, this news was devastating. I convinced myself, along with the help of family and friends, that I was not receding and that my barber was wrong. I went through a stage of denial and sli ght depression due to the thought of losing my hair at 17. However, this did not help as it put me off starting to use regaine (rogaine for those in America). Trust me, the sooner you start to use minoxidil the better. There is no shame. Once I started to use regaine I did not experience the 2 week shedding stage which led me to believe that minoxidil was not working. However, 3 months later I noticed lots of hairs growing on my temples where I had receded and my hairline was no longer looking thinner. If you're worried about losing your hair like me and do not want to go on finasteride (I live in the U.K. and I would need to be prescribed finasteride by my GP, or physician, which he was not willing to do due to my age and side effects) I would seriously recommend minoxidil - give it a go and if it doesn't work then at least you know you've tried.

I had thinning hair and shedding and this seemed to help stop it. I've also seen some regrowth, but not as much as I would have liked . People seriously need to learn to read instructions. Rogaine clearly states that for the first 2 to 4 weeks your shedding will INCREASE to clear out the weakened hair follicles to allow healthier ones to grow. Then the shedding will decrease. I had the "dead shed" for about 3 weeks and then my shedding decreased by about 60% from what I would normally get. If your shedding doesn't stop in a month it tells you to stop use. It takes me about 5 minutes to apply on my scalp in the morning and evenings. A bit of a pain, but not too bad.
